passage: Pranav had stopped counting how many times Vidya said, "If you loved me, you'd show me." First it was his phone password, then the group chat, then which shirt he should wear to Manu's birthday. "Not the blue one," she said. "Girls look at you in it." On Sunday when his friends called him for cricket, her messages piled up, angry, until he cancelled. That evening Manu texted, "You've gone quiet, yaar." Pranav stared at the screen. He realised he was afraid to put his phone down, and that being afraid didn't feel like love. He told Manu he was coming to cricket the next weekend. Then he showed his elder cousin Deepa the messages. "This is control," she said quietly. "It isn't your fault. Let's talk to your mother."

qa.q: What was the first thing Vidya asked Pranav for?
qa.a: She asked for his phone password.

qa.q: What did Pranav realise as he stared at the screen after Manu's text?
qa.a: He realised he was afraid to put his phone down and that being afraid did not feel like love.

qa.q: What steps did Pranav take that helped him?
qa.a: He stayed in touch with his friend Manu, planned to go to cricket, and showed his cousin Deepa the messages so a trusted adult could help.

qa.q: How might Manu have seen Pranav's silence?
qa.a: Manu noticed Pranav had gone quiet and seems worried about Pranav, so Manu reached out with a friendly text.

grounding: Pranav's partner demands his password, tells him what to wear and gets angry when he sees friends; he names it as control and tells a trusted person.

passage:
When I started going out with Nikhil in Class 11, I felt so special. He texted me good morning every day.
Then it changed. He asked for my passwords, "because couples don't have secrets." He told me my yellow kurta was "too much for my girlfriend" and I should wear the grey one. When I went for pani puri with Aditi and the others, he stopped talking to me for two days.
I thought that meant he loved me. That's what I told Aditi.
She said, very quietly, "Usha, that's control. Not love."
I cried that night. Then I told Amma everything while she was making rotis. She turned off the gas, sat with me on the floor and said, "This isn't your fault. We'll handle it together." She came with me to the school counsellor the next morning, and I changed all my passwords that same night.
I wear the yellow kurta a lot now. And I still see Aditi every weekend.

qa.q: What did Nikhil tell Usha about her yellow kurta?
qa.a: That it was "too much" for his girlfriend and she should wear the grey one.

qa.q: What did Usha feel after Aditi called it control?
qa.a: Usha felt shaken and sad, crying that night, as she realised what she had called love was actually control.

qa.q: Which steps helped Usha protect herself?
qa.a: Naming it as control, telling Amma the same evening, changing her passwords, seeing the counsellor and staying close to Aditi.

qa.q: How does Amma respond when Usha tells her?
qa.a: Amma stops cooking, sits with her, tells her it is not her fault, and takes her to the counsellor the next morning.

grounding: A teen whose boyfriend demands passwords and controls her clothes and friendships names it as control, keeps her friends and tells her mother.

passage:
School counsellor's note, Thursday
Ishita's friend Neelam brought her to my office during lunch. Ishita was quiet at first, turning her phone over and over.
She told me her boyfriend, Karan, checks her messages every evening and has her passwords. He tells her which clothes are "okay" and gets very angry when she spends time with friends. She said, "He does it because he loves me, right?"
I said clearly that checking her phone, choosing her clothes and cutting her off from friends is control, not a proof of love, and that none of it is her fault. She cried, then seemed relieved.
We made a plan together: she will change her passwords today, keep Neelam and her other friends close, and she agreed I could phone her mother this afternoon. I called her mother at 3 p.m.; she is coming in tomorrow morning. I will check in with Ishita before she leaves school today.

qa.q: Who brought Ishita to the counsellor's office?
What was Ishita feeling when she asked, 'He does it because he loves me, right?'
qa.a: She felt confused and anxious, unsure whether Karan's behaviour was love, and seemed relieved when it was named clearly.

qa.q: What made the counsellor's response wise?
qa.a: The counsellor named the behaviour as control, said it was not Ishita's fault, made a safety plan and phoned her mother the same day.

qa.q: How might Neelam feel after bringing Ishita in?
qa.a: Neelam likely feels worried but relieved that Ishita is getting help from a trusted adult.

grounding: A counsellor observes a teen whose boyfriend controls her passwords, clothes and friendships, names it as control and acts the same day.
